comment: The long tail of the command layer: the small Settings toggles, the
migrate bundle surface, session move / orphan adoption, the activity
cards stream, artifact-usage telemetry, the local cost report, and
the cc_doctor snapshot cache.
Every entry here is owner="command" — an ad-hoc failure raised at a
Tauri command site with no core enum behind it. Where a core enum
did exist, the conversion lifted it (`ErrorDto::from`) instead of
minting a code, which is why files that read like they should be
here are not: `cc_tips` rides `TipsError`, `available_models` rides
`SetAllowlistError`, the settings toggles ride `SettingsWriteError`,
and `migrate` / `session_move` ride their own enums for everything
except the wire values the renderer chose.
Two shapes dominate, and the split is deliberate:
- A wire discriminant the renderer sent that we do not know
(a mode, a window kind, an artifact kind, a pricing tier). The
offending value rides in params under its own name so a
localized sentence can quote it, and it is never translated —
it is a protocol token, not prose.
- A bare `std::io` / mutex failure with no enum to lift. Those
carry `detail` only, and `detail` is core's English.
Nothing here can carry a credential. The values are enum spellings,
filesystem paths, and `Display` text from a settings-file parser, a
uuid parser, or sqlite — none of the commands in this file reads a
transcript body or a keychain item.
See src-tauri/src/dto_error.rs for the consts these lock against,
and 00-foundation.json for the field contract.

codes.message: No such file or directory (os error 2)
